steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Theatre of Cruelty: not physical pain but ASSAULT ON THE SENSES — theatre should overwhelm the audience, not just tell a story.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Total theatre: using every possible means — light, sound, movement, space, colour — to create a complete sensory experience.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: No text dependence: words are not the primary medium — sound, movement and spectacle communicate beyond language.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ritual and ceremony: Artaud wanted theatre to function like a sacred ritual — transformative, primal, cathartic.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain what Artaud meant by 'Theatre of Cruelty' — why is 'cruelty' misleading? | How would you use Artaud's ideas to create a sensory, immersive experience for an audience? | Compare Artaud's approach to theatre with Brecht's. How do they want the audience to respond differently?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'Cruelty' means intensity and rigour, not physical pain. Artaud wanted theatre to be a shock to the system that awakens the audience's subconscious — an assault on the senses that strips away rational | Practical examples: surround-sound audience, performers among spectators, harsh lighting changes, drumming rhythms, exaggerated physical gesture, symbolic objects, no conventional set. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: 'Cruelty' is NOT about physical pain — always clarify this Artaud is about EXPERIENCE not INTELLECT — focus on senses and emotions Show practical techniques: soundscapes, movement, audience positioning Know that Artaud's ideas were largely unrealised — he wrote theory more than practice
